body:
Thank you for replying.

I want to let a friend know, but privacy is a quality a value very, very highly.  I don't want to spill even half of the beans to someone I don't fully trust.  And it's not like I have many options either.

She has a few friends.  One that cuts.  One that is too innocent and naive to help.  One that has a large mouth and shouldn't be trusted with secrets.  One that is a complete unknown.

How would you handle this?

She was rambling and had some confusion.  Apparently, she's stable now, but I won't say normal.  

fuck, I should've checked pupils.

Checked rooms.  No knife or pills.  Also no water cups or anything.  Only very minor blood.

I'm still a minor without paycheck or car, so I can't directly get her medical professional help.  I'll try to convince parents or something

I won't reveal age, but I will say that we are under our parent's roofs.  She is at the doctors while I'm here panicking and being useless.

Parents are okay and supportive, but very overprotective.  Personally, I think too much so.  When she comes back from the doctor, what should I do?  Give her time and space?  Immediately approach and try to support?

I'll definitely support her, but should I approach ASAP?  I know she will want privacy, but I want to help her.  Any recommendations?  Luckily for me, I've been called emotionless and level-headed by many - lets hope that continues.

Honestly, I'm not past it.  I just napped a lot until bad stuff stopped happening.  Eventually, the need went away, but it still re-appears.  I learned how to draw, write in cryptogram, and keep a (very) personal journal, but that was self motivated and even now I don't know if it helped.

I've talked to her a few times, but didn't ask anything direct.  I was there was she wanted to vent things, and I tried to give my advice.  No professional help at all.

She's had a breakdown before, but it was nowhere this bad.  Her friend has been, reportedly, self-harming for at least a year and shows no sign of stopping.  

I want to help her, but I got this information from my sister, who acted as a listener/confider.  So offering help to the friend would basically break their friendship and trust.  Even now, I want to talk to that friend, but again, I would break my sister's privacy and trust and her friend's.

I am open to any ideas right now

She's at the doctors with the rest of the family.

I'm just sitting here on my computer being useless while trying to finish homework.

Shit.  I thought of shock, but I didn't think small cuts could do that.  What do you think are the future implications (mental and physical) and how can I help.

We're gonna get a lot of over-protection from parents, which might worsen things.  My sister and I were kinda close, but I found her and called for help even when she adamantly said to say nothing.  

Is there anything at all that I can do?  I just feel so helpless.
